items.title: Bangalore University to establish placement cells in all affiliated colleges
points: Through these cells, the university will conduct placement drives, besides holding offline and online skill training essential for employment.

While the university already has a placement cell that conducts annual placement drives, and has even appointed placement officers in select affiliated colleges, these officers are currently not active.
“When enrolling in colleges, students and parents place high priority on placements.

Therefore, our university will establish placement cells in all 274 government and private colleges under its jurisdiction,” said Sarvamangala, Director, Pre-Examination Coaching Centre & Placement Cell, Bangalore University.
The university has created a separate WhatsApp group that includes the principals and placement officers from all colleges under its purview.
Some companies approach universities to impart skills as part of their Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives.
If a company wishes to visit a specific college to conduct placement activities, the university makes arrangements for that as well, Prof.

items.title: Mamata Banerjee, BJP Trade Charges Over 'Attack' On Abhishek Banerjee's Home
points: A midnight "recce", an alleged attack at 2 am, a birthday celebration disrupted before the cake could be cut, and a political confrontation that has moved from the lanes of Kalighat to the corridors of Delhi.
It began on Friday, when Abhishek Banerjee alleged that unidentified persons had been conducting reconnaissance of his office and residence for two days.

"When confronted, they claimed to be police personnel," he said on X, asking, "Why is the State Police allegedly spying on and snooping around the office and residence of an elected Member of Parliament?
"After I released the recce video this morning, my house was attacked just now, at 2 AM by BJP goons, right under the watch of the Kolkata police," he said in a post on X on Saturday.
According to police and party reports, clashes broke out between TMC workers gathering to celebrate his 39th birthday and BJP supporters between 2 am and 3:30 am.

items.title: US markets next week 9-14 Nov: After crash and bounce back, investors eye inflation data, tech earnings, and more
points: Wall Street investors are bracing for another volatile week as concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) investments, inflationary pressures and geopolitical tensions weigh on market sentiment.
Investors will closely track key US inflation data, earnings announcements from major technology companies and developments in the Middle East for fresh cues on the direction of the stock market.
The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report for October, scheduled for release on Tuesday, will be among the most closely watched economic indicators next week.
Investors will examine the inflation figures for clues about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions and the possibility of another interest rate increase in December.
According to LSEG data, interest rate futures were indicating an approximately 80% probability of a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December 8-9 meeting.
The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite closed Thursday nearly 12% below its record high of October 6.
A decline of more than 10% from a recent peak is generally considered a market correction.

items.title: Anti-Drug Activist Shot At By Gang In Punjab's Barnala
points: Chandigarh: In a chilling attack on those fighting the drug menace in Punjab, a member of an anti-drug committee was allegedly shot in the leg by four men at his home in Kaleke village of Barnala district.
The injured man, identified as Amandeep Singh alias Aman, was rushed to hospital and later referred to a super-speciality facility in Barnala.
According to Amandeep, the committee members had caught some individuals with suspected narcotic substances and immediately informed the police through emergency number 112.
Committee member Sukhchain Singh Chinna said the village panchayat, sarpanch and local organisations had jointly formed the anti-drug panel around 15-20 days ago.
He further alleged that Ranjit Singh Raju has previous cases registered against him under the Arms Act and the NDPS Act.
Meanwhile, Congress MLA Kuldeep Singh Kala Dhillon condemned the attack and warned that the party would launch a protest if the accused were not arrested within 24 hours.

items.title: Why Week After Diwali Will Be Delhi's Biggest Pollution Test
points: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has enforced Stage 3 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR.
Ahead of Diwali, the air quality in Delhi dropped significantly, triggering low visibility and foggy conditions all across the national capital.

The invocation of GRAP Stage 3 brings sweeping emergency curbs across Delhi NCR districts: complete bans on non-essential construction and demolition, strict restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel four-wheelers, and continuous deployment of…
If post-Diwali AQI breaches the 450 mark, CAQM will be forced to escalate to GRAP Stage IV, triggering commercial truck entry bans and school closures.

READ | Delhi Air Remains 'Very Poor' On Diwali Eve, Likely To Worsen Tomorrow Experts argue that halting construction projects and restricting daily commuters while simultaneously easing firecracker bans creates a glaring governance contradiction.

items.title: Drunk Man Kills Friend In Pune, Chops Off His Legs, Dumps Them In Trash
points: A 44-year-old man allegedly killed his friend with a baseball bat following an argument while they were drinking in Pune, then severed the victim's legs and dumped them at a garbage site, police said on Saturday.
The incident took place in the city's Pimple Gurav area on Friday.
The accused, identified as Pintya alias Vishnu Tanaji Kumbhar, has been arrested, they said.

According to the police, civic workers found two human legs inside a plastic sack in a roadside garbage heap on Shrinagar Lane No. 3 in the area and alerted the police, Senior Inspector Jitendra Koli of Sangvi police station said.
The number was traced to a contractor, who told police that he had given the SIM card to his employee, Anil Khade.
A photograph on his son's mobile phone helped police establish that the severed legs belonged to Khade, the official said.
They broke open the lock and found Khade's body with both legs severed and a major injury to his head.

items.title: "Fake": RBI Dismisses Claims Of New Cheque Book Rules From January
points: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Saturday dismissed as factually incorrect and misleading social media messages claiming that new cheque books with updated security standards would come into effect from January 1, 2027.

In a post on X, the central bank said it had taken note of messages circulating on social media claiming that the standard cheque books currently in use under the Cheque Truncation System (CTS) would change from December 31, 2026.
The messages claimed that cheque books featuring updated security standards would be introduced from January 1, 2027.
"RBI is not introducing any such measures with regard to the CTS cheque books," the central bank clarified.
The proposals are part of the draft Reserve Bank of India (Priority Sector Lending - Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026, aimed at strengthening oversight of agricultural lending.
Comments on the draft have been invited until November 26.

items.title: Madras HC refuses to reject Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi’s election petition
points: The Madras High Court has refused to reject an election petition filed by former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi of the DMK challenging the victory of TVK MLA Vijayakumar alias Navalapattu Viji from Thiruverumbur Assembly constituency in the 2026 election.

Kumaresh Babu said the Election Commission of India’s instructions to not engage children in election campaigns had a statutory force and, hence, the veracity of the allegation levelled against the MLA of having engaged children for his campaign could be…
The judge dismissed an application filed by the MLA to reject the petition.
Mr. Vijayakumar had won the seat by a margin of 8,705 votes.
He had secured 89,837 votes as against 81,132 votes garnered by the election petitioner who was his nearest rival candidate.

items.title: Bengaluru airport declares full emergency after security threat on Lucknow-bound IndiGo flight
points: A full emergency was declared at Kempegowda International Airport (Terminal 1) in Bengaluru on Saturday after a suspected hijack threat message was discovered inside the lavatory of an IndiGo flight scheduled for Lucknow.
IndiGo flight 6E-451 was en route from Bengaluru to Lucknow when crew members detected the threatening note inside the aircraft's washroom.
Adhering to strict safety protocols, the pilots immediately turned the aircraft back to Bengaluru to initiate security procedures.
Upon landing, airport security personnel and aviation law enforcement authorities took control of the aircraft, isolating it to execute thorough anti-sabotage and safety sweeps.
Addressing the security threat, an IndiGo spokesperson issued an official press statement.
"A security threat was reported onboard IndiGo flight 6E 451, operating from Bengaluru to Lucknow on 07 November 2026.

In line with Standard Operating Procedure, the relevant authorities were informed immediately and the pilots decided to return to origin to carry out the necessary security checks, as per protocol," read the statement.

items.title: 'Ignore, See Consequences': IndiGo Flight Returns To Bengaluru After Hijack Threat Note Found In Toilet
points: A Bengaluru-Lucknow IndiGo flight was forced to return to the Kempegowda International Airport after a handwritten note threatening a hijacking was found inside the aircraft's toilet.
The flight, 6E451, which took off from Bengaluru at 5:50 pm with 178 passengers on board, was mid-air when a passenger spotted the note in the toilet.
It read, "This plane is going to get hijacked exactly at 06:30.
Ignore and see the consequences." The passenger alerted the crew; the pilot informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) and returned the aircraft to Bengaluru as a precautionary measure.
After landing, all passengers were deboarded, and security personnel conducted thorough checks of the aircraft.
The flight was to take off again only after security clearances, as per the latest update.

IndiGo issued a press statement that read, "In line with Standard Operating Procedure, the relevant authorities were informed immediately and the pilots decided to return to origin to carry out the necessary security checks, as per protocol...

points: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) conducted a trial run of a train on the test track at the Byappanahalli depot on Saturday as part of preparations for the much-awaited Blue Line.
The trial involved checking electrical systems, assessing the readiness of rolling stock and identifying possible infringements along the track.
BMRCL is expected to move testing to the main line shortly.
An official said that the testing would resume next week, subject to the availability of workers following Deepavali.
Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) has manufactured the driverless trainset for the Blue Line.
The Blue Line, comprising Metro Phases 2A and 2B, is a major infrastructure project connecting the city with Kempegowda International Airport.

The majority shareholder plans to reduce its stake in HCCH from 60% to approximately 45% following the share sale.
Jubilant Beverages, which holds the remaining 40% stake in the company, will not participate in the proposed IPO.
The IPO filing comes months after Coca-Cola announced in June that it was exploring a potential stock market listing of HCCH in 2027.

The issue will be managed by a consortium of investment banks, including Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, Citigroup Global Markets India, JP Morgan India, Morgan Stanley India Company, Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs (India) Securities and IIFL Capital Services.
As of June 30, 2026, its product portfolio comprised 41 beverages, including popular brands such as Coca-Cola, Thums Up, Sprite and Maaza.

points: Yet, the accused in the alleged Rajajinagar murders, Indushekhar, was never detected.
Indushekar, prime accused in the case where he killed his wife and six others from her family, resided in a building near (barely 100 metres) the famous Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar.

items.title: Habitual offender arrested for murdering 65-year-old woman in Bengaluru
points: The Kengeri police have arrested a habitual offender for allegedly murdering a 65-year-old woman who was sleeping outside a temple and robbing her of cash and a gold ring in Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout.
The deceased, Narayanamma, was found dead in front of the Pataladamma Temple at Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout, Konasandra, within Kengeri police station limits, on November 3.
According to the police, Narayanamma had left her house due to family problems and had been sleeping outside the temple for the past few days.
A local resident who noticed her body informed her son, who arrived at the spot and identified her.
The Kengeri police initially registered an unnatural death report based on his complaint.
During the investigation, police apprehended a suspicious person moving around Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout on Friday.
In the early hours of November 3, he allegedly went to the spot, covered her mouth, assaulted her and robbed her of the cash she was carrying and a gold ring before fleeing, leaving her dead.

items.title: No complete closure of Ballari Road for 18 months for elevated corridor work: BDA
points: Flyover work in progress, near Hebbal, by the Bengaluru Development Authority (BDA) in Bengaluru on November 7, 2026. | Photo Credit: ALLEN EGENUSE J.

The Hebbal Flyover and Ballari Road corridor will not be completely closed for 18 months to facilitate the construction of the elevated corridor, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) clarified on Saturday (November 7).
Meanwhile, the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) said vehicular movement would continue with limited lane restrictions and phased traffic diversions.

The elevated corridor is part of the BDA’s larger Integrated Tunnel and Elevated Corridor Project, aimed at easing congestion along the city’s crucial northern corridor connecting Bengaluru with Kempegowda International Airport.
The BTP sources said restrictions would apply only to the movement of heavy vehicles between 6 a.m. and 8 p.m., while other motorists would merely be “advised” to take alternative routes.
The BDA said barricading would be restricted to a lane approximately 4.5 metres wide, affecting only one of the three existing lanes in each direction.

items.title: 'Tough' stance on Kishau Dam project laid ground for victory in BBMB dues case: Himachal CM
points: Mr. Sukhu said that during meetings with the Union Power Minister and officials, he had consistently raised the issue of dues arising from BBMB projects and made it clear that the rights of Himachal Pradesh in the matter must be resolved before any further…

He said the State asserted that it would not share the cost of the 440-MW Kishau Dam project, and the Haryana government assured that it would file an affidavit in the Supreme Court in favour of Himachal Pradesh for the release of arrears of its power…
Ruling in favour of Himachal Pradesh, the Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) said the hill State would get 11,973 MU of electricity from Punjab and Haryana over 20 years.
The arrangement will be as per a 2011 Supreme Court verdict settling power dues arising out of Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydro projects since 1966 at the rate of 7.19%.

items.title: A woman stitches her way into the male-dominated ritual tradition of Theyyam
points: Priya stitches traditional costumes worn by Theyyam performers. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT In the ritual world of Theyyam, where women rarely find a place in the traditional roles, 41-year-old M.
Priya of Kannayi Mukkottu near Payyannur has carved out a distinctive space for herself.
Rather than performing rituals, she stitches costumes and decorative garments that transforms male performers into divine figures in the Malabar’s sacred groves and temples.
For Priya, the Theyyam season is also the busiest time of the year.
Beginning in November and continuing until March or May, depending on the festival calendar, it keeps her sewing machine busy.
Although she has been involved in the work for over 15 years, Ms. Priya has never ventured into conventional tailoring.
Among the items she makes are kaani, kachunkaraa, Valinjery, kuttithaya and Velimban, Kayipodip, Thalachut besides several other components of Theyyam attire.
Ms. Priya spends her evenings from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. at the sewing machine.

items.title: ‘Apologise to Ram Bhakts first’: Yogi Adityanath ahead of Akhilesh Yadav's visit to Ayodhya
points: Ahead of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's proposed visit to Ram temple in Ayodhya, chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday sought an apology from those who opened fire at karsevaks in 1990.
Without addressing Yadav directly, Adityanath demanded that an apology be tendered to 'Ram Bhakts' before visiting Ayodhya.
The chief minister was referring to the firing that took place on October 30 and November 2 in 1990, during the government of Samajwadi Party patriarch Mulayam Singh Yadav.
Akhilesh Yadav is set to visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya with his family on December 12.
This will be his first visit to the temple since its consecration in January 2024.

Taking aim at Yadav, Adityanath said, "Tender an apology to Ram Bhakts first for firing on karsevaks before coming to Ayodhya." The chief minister was addressing seers at Ram Katha Park in Ayodhya at the 10th edition of Deepotsav.
Adityanath credited 10 years of Deepotsav, the construction of the Ram temple and infrastructure development for restoring Ayodhya's ancient glory.

items.title: Manipur gets Northeast’s first AI-enabled career intelligence hub
points: Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh interacting with school students at a science event in Imphal on November 7.
Conflict-scarred Manipur has become the first State in the northeastern region to get an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled facility that aims to mould careers.

Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh on Saturday (November 7, 2026) inaugurated the AI-enabled Career Intelligence Hub at the Tamphasana Girls’ Higher Secondary School in Imphal, the State’s capital.

Established under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme as the region’s first-of-its-kind facility, the initiative marked a “significant step towards integrating AI into the education and career guidance ecosystem in the State”.

Earlier, the Chief Minister lauded two districts—Imphal West and Pherzawl—for achieving ‘surakshit (safe)’ status in October under the National AIDS Control Organisation’s (NACO) Mobilisation for AIDS Suraksha initiative.

items.title: YSRCP suffers setback in Kadapa ZPTC polls
points: The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) suffered another setback in the Kadapa ZPTC elections, soon after its poor performance in the municipal polls.
Of the 39 ZPTC seats in the district, 23 were won unanimously before polling.
Elections were held for the remaining 16 seats on Thursday, of which the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) won 10 and the Jana Sena Party (JSP) one.
The YSRCP managed to secure only two seats, both in the Pulivendula Assembly constituency.
Of the four ZPTC seats in Pulivendula, the TDP won Lingala and Pulivendula mandals, while the YSRCP emerged victorious in Vempalli and Vemula mandals.
The results for three other ZPTC seats were pending at the time of filing this report.
Of the 407 MPTC seats in the district, alliance candidates were elected unanimously in 352.
Polling was held for 55 seats, but results for 28 were yet to be declared.

items.title: Two murder-for-gain cases cracked, four held for ‘killing’ 103-year-old, 80-year-old women
points: Two murder-for-gain cases involving the killing of two elderly women, aged 103 and 80, in Vachunur village of Thimmapur mandal in August and October this year have been solved, with the LMD police arresting four accused in Karimnagar on Saturday.
The police identified the arrested persons as Madduri Sai, 24, Kinnera Raju, 25, A.
Pavan Kumar, 28, all residents of Vachunur.

According to the police, the accused allegedly suffocated Bhudamma, 103, at her residence on August 16, and murdered another elderly woman, Lachavva, 80, who also lived alone in the same village on October 31.
They allegedly stole gold ornaments belonging to both victims.
An intensive investigation by the LMD police into the two cases led to the identification and arrest of the four accused.
Karimnagar Police Commissioner Gaush Alam commended the local police for their coordinated efforts in solving both murder-for-gain cases and apprehending the accused.

items.title: TDP-led alliance sweeps Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC elections, secures landslide victory; YSRCP lags behind
points: The Telugu Desam Party (TDP)-led alliance in Andhra Pradesh registered a landslide victory in the elections to the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs), according to results announced by…

As vote counting was still underway, the SEC released figures at 9 pm showing that the Telugu Desam Party and its alliance partners, the Jana Sena Party and the Bharatiya Janata Party, had together won 273 of the 582 ZPTC seats and 5,597 of the 7,767 MPTC…
The TDP emerged as the dominant party, winning 229 ZPTC seats and 4,823 MPTC seats, including those declared unopposed.
Its alliance partner, the Jana Sena Party, secured 36 ZPTC seats and 644 MPTC seats, while the BJP won eight ZPTC seats and 130 MPTC seats.
The TDP's performance was particularly striking in the MPTC elections, where it secured 4,823 seats, far ahead of the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which managed 1,050 seats.

items.title: Over 100 Men Surround Amritsar House, Open Fire. Several Injured
points: Around 100 armed men allegedly surrounded a house and opened fire in broad daylight in Punjab's Amritsar district.
The attack, reportedly triggered by an old rivalry between two groups, left a young man with a bullet injury and several others injured.
The injured man, identified as Sandeep Singh, was shot in the leg and also sustained injuries from sharp-edged weapons, including a kirpan and datar.
He was rushed to Guru Nanak Dev Hospital in Amritsar for treatment.

Recounting the incident, Vishal Singh, a member of the victim's family, alleged that the attackers arrived in a large group, surrounded their house in Akalgarh Dhapian village in Amritsar's Jandiala area and launched a coordinated assault using firearms…
Alleging that the rival group had planned the attack, Vishal named several individuals, including Maninder, Gurmukh, Kuki from the Tarn Taran/Tarapur area and Akash, along with unidentified men.
A bullet reportedly fired from a .30-bore pistol struck Sandeep in the leg, while pellets from a 12-bore gun were also fired during the confrontation.

items.title: TDP dominates Rajam constituency with major wins in ZPTC and MPTC elections
points: Newly elected ZPTC and MMPTC members felicitating Rajam TDP MLA Kondru Murali Mohan in Vizianagaram district on Saturday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) received the biggest shock in Rajam constituency where it was defeated in…

TDP MLA Kondru Murali Mohan said that the TDP registered spectacular victories in his constituency with the effective implementation of welfare schemes and developmental works taken up with ₹400 crore.
Chandrababu Naidu and TDP national general secretary Nara Lokesh for giving special focus to Rajam in the last few years.
“YSRCP won Rajam Assembly segment in 2014 and 2019 also but tasted bitter defeat in 2024 Assembly elections and now in local body elections.
The people would repose faith in TDP in 2029 general elections also,” said Mr. Murali Mohan while speaking to media here.

items.title: CJP founder launches scathing attack on Central government
points: Addressing a protest named ‘Jantar Mantar @ Kochi’ demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Mr. Dipke stressed that “Modi will go out in 2029.” “I want…
Any change in government must occur through the democratic electoral system, even if we have to wait till the 2029 elections,” Mr. Dipke said, carrying a tricolour.
It was Mr. Dipke’s first public address in Keralam.
“Why is Gyanesh Kumar so important to Modi that he is waging a war against the youth of his own country?” the CJP leader asked, referring to the use of State forces against the protests in Delhi.
Praising Keralam’s social conditions, he said India would have achieved a developed nation status long ago had other States followed the State’s lead in education and literacy.

items.title: Bihar’s Ranivas Mound declared monument of national importance
points: An ancient mound in Bihar's East Champaran district has been declared an archaeological site of national importance through a central government notification.

The site – Ranivas Mound, at Kesariya – is spread over 1.63 acres and is under the ownership of the Bihar government, reads the gazette notification dated November 4 that was issued by the Ministry of Culture.

Copies of the said notification were made available to the public on June 8, 2026 and "no objection has been received" from any person with regard to the declaration by the central government, said the notification signed by Archaeological Survey of India…
A copy of the notification was affixed at a conspicuous place as required under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958.
A recommendation for listing the ancient Ranivas mound in Bihar as a centrally protected monument was sent to ASI headquarters in Delhi in 2021, a senior official told PTI in September 2022.

items.title: Biswajit Basu becomes fourth retired judge to resign from West Bengal SIR tribunal
points: The SIR process in the State was held from October 2025 to February 2026, just before the Assembly election Over 91 lakh electors were deleted from the electoral rolls; they accounted for about 13% of all voters in the State before the start of the SIR.

File | Photo Credit: PTI Retired Calcutta High Court judge Biswajit Basu resigned from a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) tribunal in West Bengal on Saturday (November 7, 2026), citing personal reasons.

He became the fourth judge to step down, raising questions about the functioning of the 19 tribunals tasked with hearing 38 lakh appeals by voters deleted from the electoral rolls during the SIR process in the State.
Justice (retd.) Basu had previously expressed unhappiness about the functioning of the tribunals, saying, “Resolving lakhs of cases in this manner is a little difficult.

items.title: Man Run Over By Speeding Bus While Crossing Road In Gurugram
points: A man died while crossing the road after allegedly being run over by a speeding bus near Chhath Ghat at Gurugram's Baba Prakash Puri Chowk on Saturday, police said.
Upon receiving information, a police team arrived at the scene, sent the body to the mortuary, and has initiated further action, they said.
The identity of the victim has not yet been established, the police said, adding that efforts are underway to identify him.
According to locals, the incident occurred around 2 pm on Saturday.
The accident was so severe that the individual died on the spot.
Traces of blood were visible at the scene, and the body of the victim had been covered with a blanket.
(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: US Market Outlook: Support to give a relief
points: The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and NASDAQ Composite index continues to get beaten down.
The Dow Jones, down 0.94 per cent, fell for the second consecutive week.
The S&P 500 and NASDAQ Composite indices closed in negative for the fourth consecutive week.
They were down 2.68 per cent and 3.37 per cent, respectively.
The sharp fall after the initial surge to 53,716 keeps the broader bias negative.
The Dow Jones can fall to 50,700 or 50,400 from here.
In case the index fails to bounce back from the 7,300-7,280 support zone, then an extended fall to 7,200 can be seen.
A bounce from the 24,100-24,000 support zone can take the NASDAQ Composite index up to 25,200 or even 25,500.

items.title: Rajasthan bags national award for performance in renewable energy framework
points: Rajasthan has received a national award for its outstanding performance under the Renewable Energy State Assessment Framework (RE-SAF), developed by the Union Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
Radhakrishnan gave away the award at a function in New Delhi over the weekend.
Rajasthan Minister of State for Energy Heeralal Nagar, who received the award, said the State had emerged as the country’s largest green energy hub over the years.
“The State now has an installed renewable energy capacity of 51.6 GW and a solar power capacity of 45 GW,” Mr. Nagar said.
Mr. Nagar said the State was playing a “pivotal role” in achieving the national goal of 500 GW non-fossil fuel-based installed power capacity by 2030.
With the new milestones in the renewable energy sector, Rajasthan had received top honours under RE-SAF developed by the Union Ministry in collaboration with the Power Finance Corporation, he said.

items.title: Index Outlook: Early Diwali celebration
points: Sparkling fireworks isolated on black background istockphoto for BL | Photo Credit: Ina Fischer Market has given a nice Diwali gift to everyone in the form of a strong 8 per cent rally last week.
The equity segment saw a net inflow of about $4.11 billion last week.
In case Nifty breaks above 25,050 from here itself, then 25,500-25,700 can be seen this week.
Medium-term view: The rise within the 22,000-26,500 range is happening much faster than expected.
At this pace, Nifty can reach 26,500, the upper end of the range much quicker.
Failure to breach 26,500 can drag the Nifty down to 25,000 or even lower.
A reversal from this resistance can drag the Nifty Bank index down to 57,800-57,700.
That leg of upmove can take the Nifty Bank index higher to 61,200.

items.title: Crude Check: Bears make their move
points: Oil prices crashed last week, posting their biggest weekly loss since March 2020.
Brent crude oil futures on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) ($98.30/barrel) tumbled 13.3 per cent, slipping below the $100-mark and snapping the recovery seen in recent weeks.
Crude oil (Nov) futures in the domestic market (₹8,459/barrel) plunged 14.9 per cent.
Brent crude futures fell sharply, marking a two-month low of $93.22 on Wednesday.
However, despite witnessing one of the steepest declines in recent years, the contract managed to close above the crucial support at $98.
For the outlook to turn positive, Brent futures should break above $105 and sustain the rally.
Crude oil (Nov) futures crashed below ₹9,000 and is now trading beneath both the 21- and 50-day moving averages, indicating a deterioration in the short-term trend.
Crude oil futures could resume the decline either from the current level or after a rebound towards ₹9,000.

items.title: Bullion Cues: Supports fuel a rebound
points: Gold ($4,070.60/ounce) and silver ($51.70/ounce) gained 5 per cent and 5.8 per cent, respectively.
In the domestic market, gold futures (₹1,42,167/10 gram) gained 2.7 per cent, while silver futures (₹1,84,787/kg) rose 3.2 per cent.

The gains were relatively modest as the rupee strengthened 1.1 per cent against the dollar last week Gold (Dec) futures rallied from the support at ₹1,38,000, aided by a recovery in global prices from $3,850.
With international gold reclaiming $4,000, further gains appear likely, although hurdles remain.
On the downside, supports are at ₹1,40,000 and ₹1,38,000.
Silver (Dec) futures marked a lower low of ₹1,75,251 on Tuesday before recovering.
A breakout above ₹2,00,000 can strengthen the upswing, potentially taking the price to ₹2,10,000 in the near term.
Conversely, a fall below the support at ₹1,75,000 can trigger a deeper decline to ₹1,67,000.

items.title: AAP Invokes 1984 Riots In Attack On Rahul Gandhi After His 'Drinking' Jab At Bhagwant Mann
points: After Rahul Gandhi accused Mann of remaining under the influence of alcohol and failing to tackle Punjab's drug problem, AAP has released a fresh video on its social media handle, accusing the Congress leader of targeting not just the chief minister but…
The video features references to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, showing visuals of Sikhs being targeted during the violence.
The latest video marks a significant escalation in AAP's response.
The party's social media handle took a 'Pappu' jibe at the Congress leader.
AAP leaders also accused Gandhi of resorting to personal attacks, questioning why he was targeting Mann instead of focusing on a political debate over Punjab's issues.

The controversy began when Rahul Gandhi, addressing the Congress's Insaaf Rally in Sangrur on November 4, recalled his days in Parliament with Mann and alleged that he could smell alcohol on the comedian-turned-politician even in the morning.
Gandhi questioned how Mann could lead the fight against drugs if he himself was allegedly intoxicated every evening.

items.title: Under-construction roof of school auditorium collapses in Kanjiramkulam
points: Updated - November 07, 2026 10:09 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram An under-construction roof of an auditorium at an aided school near Neyyattinkara collapsed on Saturday morning.
As it was not a working day, no students were around.
The workers involved in the roofing work also had an escape as they had moved on to another section.
The incident occurred at PKS Higher Secondary School, Kanjiramkulam.
The auditorium had a roofing sheet, and work was on to replace it with a concrete roof.
Since the auditorium was large, work on putting up a concrete roof had begun on a portion of it in the morning.
However, not much later the roof collapsed.
General Education department officials suspect that supporting beams made of wood collapsed, bringing down the roof.

items.title: Kerala Water Authority intensifies action against encroachments on Pipeline Road
points: The water utility said on Saturday that it has intensified action against encroachers.
As part of the drive, illegal structures were removed at the Vazhayila junction on Friday.
“These measures are being taken to protect the Pipeline Road and the allied KWA assets and to ensure access for carrying out repairs and maintenance works,” the KWA said.
The Pipeline Road is important for the KWA as the transmission main carrying water from Aruvikkara to the capital city passes through it.
KWA officials are also serving notices to encroachers under provisions of the KWA (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupation and Removal of Unauthorised Constructions) Regulations, 2014.
Failure to vacate within the 30-day deadline prescribed in that order will attract eviction measures with the assistance of the police, according to KWA.
In August this year, the KWA had ordered that all permanent, semi-permanent and other encroachments be removed from the Pipeline Road in Kochi.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu: Andhra Pradesh CM orders swift power restoration, price control measures
points: Chandrababu Naidu | Photo Credit: File Photo Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N.

Chandrababu Naidu has directed the officials to expedite relief and restoration operations in the areas affected by Cyclone Murasu, ensure prompt financial assistance to the victims and take steps to prevent a rise in the prices of essential commodities.

During a review meeting at his camp office on Saturday, Mr. Naidu assessed the damage caused by Cyclone Murasu and enquired about the progress of power restoration works, distribution of essential supplies and assessment of crop losses.
The officials informed Mr. Naidu that nearly 92% of the assessment of horticultural crop damage had been completed, while the same for agricultural crops would be completed by November 9.
Detailing the power restoration work, the officials said around 30,000 electricity poles damaged during Cyclone Arnav had been repaired, and power supply had been restored to all affected villages.
Following Cyclone Murasu, the restoration work is underway in 1,825 villages, with 7,850 damaged poles already repaired, they said.

items.title: Gyanesh Kumar will soon be forced to step down, says K.C. Venugopal
points: Venugopal, Deepa Dasmunshi and others at the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally organised by the District Congress Committee at Kozhikode Beach on Saturday. | Photo Credit: K.
Ragesh Amid the Opposition’s intensifying protests over alleged electoral malpractice, All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary K.C.
Venugopal has said that Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar would soon be forced to step down.

Referring to the Haryana Assembly election, in which the Congress lost by a margin of 0.4 percentage points despite predictions of a party wave, he said a booth-level investigation led by Rahul Gandhi had exposed large-scale vote theft.
Mr. Venugopal levelled serious allegations against Mr. Kumar, accusing him of corruption during his earlier stints as Ernakulam District Collector and Public Works department Secretary in Kerala.

Criticising the 2023 amendment to the law governing the appointment of election commissioners, he alleged that the Modi government had granted them legal immunity even greater than that enjoyed by the President, Prime Minister, and Chief Justice of India.

items.title: Private credit defaults record largest quarterly jump, KBRA says
points: The number of companies defaulting on their private credit debt rose by the most on a quarterly basis, as smaller borrowers grow increasingly vulnerable to operating, liquidity and leverage pressures, according to Kroll Bond Rating Agency.
A record 112 borrowers with private debt defaulted on their obligations, marking a 22% increase from the previous quarter, KBRA said in a report Thursday.
The firm analyzed more than 3,000 middle-market companies — with over $1.4 trillion of direct-lending debt — in the last 12 months through September.
Lower middle-market firms typically have $100 million or less in debt and Ebitda of $25 million or less, as defined by KBRA.
Those in the core category have more than $100 million but less than $500 million of debt.
Their Ebitda exceeds $25 million but is less than $75 million.
By count, about 5.8% of the lower middle-market firms analyzed by KBRA defaulted in the twelve months through the third quarter, compared to 4.8% in the prior quarter.

items.title: Devendra Fadnavis To Spend Diwali With Drought-Affected Farmers In Nagpur
points: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday said he will celebrate Diwali with farmers in Lohari Savanga village in Nagpur's Narkhed taluka to "boost their morale" amid drought in the state.
"Maharashtra is experiencing severe drought this year, and farmers are facing a major crisis.
Therefore, all ministers have collectively decided that this time, we will celebrate Diwali by visiting villages and spending time with farmers," he told reporters.
"We will interact with farmers, sit together with them, and, in a way, make an effort to boost their morale through this initiative," he added.
Fadnavis said there was no "immediate solution" to a crisis like drought, but asserted his government would provide all possible assistance to support farmers.
"At the same time, we want to ensure that their morale remains high and they feel the government stands with them.
This is why we have taken this decision (celebrating Diwali with farmers)," the chief minister added.

items.title: NDA dominates Kurnool, Nandyal ZPTC and MPTC polls; YSRCP puts up fight in Anantapur
points: The NDA parties won a majority of the ZPTC and MPTC seats in Kurnool and Nandyal districts, while the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) put up a strong fight against the ruling coalition in Anantapur district, according to the latest reports.
In Anantapur district, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) won 175 of the 357 MPTC seats and was leading in another 85.
The YSRCP won 34 seats and was leading in 37 others.
In the erstwhile combined Kurnool district, the TDP-led NDA secured 48 of the 54 ZPTC seats, while the YSRCP won around six.
According to the latest reports, the alliance candidates also bagged nearly 90% of the MPTC seats.
In Kurnool district, none of the 26 ZPTC seats was elected unanimously and all went to polls.
In Nandyal district, eight of the 28 ZPTC seats were elected unanimously, while elections were held for the remaining 20.

items.title: AIDSO protests against Congress government’s move to allow adoption of govt. schools by private institutions
points: She alleged that the government had held a meeting at Vidhana Soudha on November 4 to facilitate the handing over of government schools to private institutions and corporate companies, with 2,000 schools proposed to be taken up in the first phase.
She termed the move a betrayal of the people.
Ms. Meti also criticised Chief Minister D.K.

Shivakumar and the government representatives for allegedly making derogatory remarks about government school teachers and blaming them for declining educational standards, while overlooking shortcomings in its own policies.
She said the government was proposing that private institutions adopt three government schools each, with the provision to name the schools after the adopting institutions.
Other proposals reportedly included deputing teachers from private schools and providing old buses, laboratory equipment and computers.

Ms. Meti alleged that 14 government schools had already been merged with the KPS at Hegganuru in Kanakapura, Bengaluru South district, contradicting the government’s assurance that no government school would be closed.

items.title: NDA wins large number of MPTC seats in Godavari region
points: Mr. Raja and his supporters sought a recount after the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) candidate secured a huge lead in the fourth round of counting.
The YSRCP had secured a substantial majority in the first three rounds.
Later, Mr. Raja and his supporters were arrested, following which the counting resumed.
Meanwhile, counting of ZPTC votes continued at all counting centres across the Godavari region till 9 p.m., with police personnel deployed to prevent any untoward incidents.
In the MPTC elections, the NDA partners, the TDP and the Jana Sena Party, secured victories in a large number of seats.
The winners were advised against taking out victory rallies to prevent any untoward incidents in the Godavari region.

items.title: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke predicts ‘Modi govt’s defeat in 2029’ at anti-SIR rally in Kochi: ‘He will definitely go’
points: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday predicted that the Modi government would be voted out of power in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections and urged people to prepare for a change of government at the Centre.
Track live updates on anti-SIR stir in Kochi Referring to the BJP's assertion that Modi would remain in power, Dipke said, "Be prepared for 2029.
He will definitely go." He repeatedly asked the gathering whether Modi would lose power in 2029, drawing cheers from the protesters.
"The change in the government will only happen through elections," he said, adding that the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was necessary to ensure a fair electoral process.
Dipke said the country was founded on the ideals of three leaders -- B R Ambedkar, Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru.
Rejecting allegations that the CJP was receiving foreign funds or working to destabilise India, Dipke accused Modi of acting at the behest of foreign powers, particularly US President Donald Trump.

items.title: Hard work key to success, says Arvind Bellad
points: Hubballi-Dharwad West MLA Arvind Bellad speaking at the induction programme at Bright Business School in Hubballi recently. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Hubballi-Dharwad West MLA Arvind Bellad has advised MBA students to work hard and make the best…
Inaugurating the induction programme, UDAAN 2K26, for new MBA students at Bright Business School in Hubballi recently, he said there was no shortcut to success.
Recalling his father’s advice, he said intelligence alone was insufficient, and hard work was essential.
Mr. Bellad urged students to learn through interactions with people, introspect on their shortcomings and make the best use of their MBA education.
Former CEO of Reliance Jio Infocom Ltd. , Mumbai, Sanjeev Ghanate said the next two years would be crucial for students to prepare for careers in the corporate sector.
He urged them to make effective use of faculty guidance and work towards becoming successful managers and leaders.
B-School director Prasad Roodagi welcomed the gathering, while governing council chairman G.B.

items.title: Rajajinagar murders: Police retrieve two more bodies from Tamil Nadu; search on for four
points: Sunita, 40, was the wife of the prime accused, Indushekhar, 52, while Roopavathi, 65, was his mother-in-law.

On Friday (November 6), the Bengaluru police arrested Indushekhar, who allegedly killed his wife and six members of her family, including a seven-year-old boy, and disposed of the bodies over a span of 18 days.
An 11-year-old boy, a relative of the accused, was rescued.
According to sources, Sunita was murdered on October 16 and Roopavathi the following day.
Considering the importance of the accused’s physical presence during the search operations, the police have secured 12 days of his custody.

One of the major questions confronting investigators concerns the logistics and method used to bring the bodies down from the second floor of the building located near the busy Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar.
A strong suspicion is that he may have used ropes to lower the bodies to the ground, possibly with the help of his 17-year-old daughter, who is also an accused in the case.

items.title: YSRCP wins key ZPTC seats in Saluru
points: YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) won Salur and Makkuva ZPTC seats that are part of Saluru Assembly segment represented by Minister of Tribal Welfare Gummadi Sandhya Rani.
YSRCP candidate Dandi Anantakumari secured 14,335 votes and TDP nominee Appikonda Ramadevi polled 14,270 votes.
As the winning margin was only 65 votes, TDP agents requested for recounting, following which YSRCP leader secured the same votes and was declared elected.
In Makkuva Assembly segment, YSRCP nominee Marri Paramma defeated her nearest TDP rival S.
The YSRCP had won 13 wards out of 32 in Saluru municipal elections.
TDP was confined to 11 wards and JSP got four seats.
JSP chairperson candidate Gorle Vijaya Kumari defeated YSRCP nominee Ribka Rani with a slight margin in municipal elections.
Former Deputy Chief Minister Peedika Rajanna Dora congratulated newly elected ZPTCs and MPTC members and said that YSRCP would get more strength by 2029 Assembly elections.

items.title: Alleged habitual offender sent to jail under KAAPA
points: A 40-year-old alleged habitual offender was sent to the Kannur Central Prison under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA) after being linked to scores of theft cases in the region. ​The man was identified as Mujeeb, a resident of…
He is listed as a known offender at the Kunnamangalam police station in Kozhikode.

The police said Mujeeb faces more than 35 cases across Kozhikode and Malappuram districts, with cases registered at stations including Kondotty, Karipur, Areekode, Edacherry, Koduvally, Atholi, Kunnamangalam, Pantheerankavu, Town, Nadakkavu and Vellayil.
The allegations against him include snatching cash and jewellery, stealing vehicles parked in public places and breaking into locked shops.
Following a preliminary report by the local sub-inspector and a recommendation from Deputy Commissioner of Police (Kozhikode City) Padam Singh, District Collector M.S.
Madhavikutty ordered his transfer to the Kannur Central Prison.
